coverage_summary: VERDICT: NO-GO FOR IMPLEMENTATION HANDOFF. Reviewed plan.md, all eight phase files, ADR-0005, both judge reports, both saved research reports, the scout report, and the pinned embedded-tls 0.19 client-certificate API. Phase 5 is correctly software-only and Phases 6–8 are correctly hardware-gated; dependencies are mostly transitively coherent. No Critical defect survives because the plan is pending and the current relay remains fail-closed. Seven High and two Medium defects remain, so it is not possible to state that no Critical/High remains. Revise and re-red-team before implementation.

findings.title: Relay readiness remains coupled to the existing C2C root lifecycle
findings.summary: Phase 1 creates a distinct P-256 identity but reuses existing assessment/epoch/rotation primitives, while Phase 7 is relay-P-256-only. A coarse Ready result can authorize the wrong capability or force a relay-only provider to pretend it satisfies X25519.

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: A distinct public-key type does not stop shared readiness state from substituting one purpose for another.

evidence.label: Required revision
evidence.explanation: Freeze independent C2cX25519Status and RelayP256Status with separate algorithm, generation, policy epoch, provider identity and readiness. Permit Phase 7 to implement relay only; add cross-purpose readiness/rotation/error-precedence tests.

optionalProperties.release_gate: Neither capability becomes Ready because the other is healthy.

findings.title: The CSR/TPM lane can recreate a generic P-256 signing oracle
findings.summary: Phase 3 constrains CSR construction only in KMS, Phase 6 permits a TPM profile, and Phase 7 never requires the protected device to reconstruct or validate the exact CertificationRequestInfo. A compromised provisioner, KMS, AP, or generic TPM signing route can feed an attacker-chosen digest to the durable relay key.

locations.role: KMS-only CSR construction and ambiguous enrollment authority

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: KMS canonicalization protects an honest KMS from hostile IPC; it does not constrain the RoT when KMS/AP is compromised.

evidence.label: Required revision
evidence.explanation: The protected root must construct the frozen CRI from a profile ID and RoT-derived fields, or enforce every field before signing. Reject arbitrary TPM2_Sign/digest routes. Define one generation-bound enrollment capability; bind and bound the one-shot handle; test raw digest, changed profile, stale handle and caller restart.

optionalProperties.release_gate: A compromised AP/KMS obtains only exact TLS CertificateVerify and frozen relay-CSR signatures.

findings.title: The certificate state machine cannot represent safe renewal overlap
findings.summary: One linear Unprovisioned→Pending→Active→Retiring/Revoked state plus CSR denial in Active cannot represent an active generation and pending successor. The torn-update result permits the old profile without defining when revocation overrides availability.

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: A single state cannot express Active(g)+Pending(g+1), and 'old valid profile or fail closed' does not say whether a revoked generation can survive.

evidence.label: Required revision
evidence.explanation: Specify a per-generation two-slot state machine with Active, Pending, optional Retiring, revoked floor/set, CA version, manifest digest and commit marker. Freeze actors, transition and write order, successor-CSR rules, overlap deadline, recovery at every crash point, and make revocation beat availability.

optionalProperties.release_gate: An old profile is usable only if explicitly authorized and above all protected floors.

findings.title: Mounted relay trust and revocation state has no authenticated anti-rollback binding
findings.summary: External client trust and relay denylist manifests are versioned but not bound to protected monotonic state. Phase 6 omits endpoint/hostname, server CA set, overlap window, full profile digest and relay denylist version, so replay can restore a compromised CA or revoked NodeId.

evidence.label: Execution path
evidence.explanation: An older valid manifest can match KMS key metadata while regressing relay trust or denylist policy.

evidence.label: Required revision
evidence.explanation: Use canonical signed manifests and protected monotonic floors/digests for the full client profile and relay-side CA/denylist state. Bind client profile digest into signer readiness; specify signer authority, atomic swap, staleness/offline/recovery rules, and inject old versions on both sides.

optionalProperties.release_gate: No old manifest restores a CA, endpoint, certificate or NodeId below the protected floor.

findings.title: Certificate validity checks have no trusted time source or rollback policy
findings.summary: Phases 3 and 4 require expired/future and server-validity rejection, but no plan file defines authenticated time, boot-without-time behavior, or clock rollback protection. A reset or controlled clock can revalidate expired or not-yet-valid certificates.

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: The plan names validity checks but no trusted clock, last-known-good state, skew or fail-closed startup behavior.

evidence.label: Required revision
evidence.explanation: Before Phase 3, select the production time authority and define trust path, protected last-known-good state, rollback/forward-jump limits, boot/offline behavior and CA-overlap interaction. QEMU uses an injected clock. Test no-time, reboot, clock jumps, stale signed time and expiry during handshake.

optionalProperties.release_gate: No validity check uses a default epoch, unchecked wall clock or ignore-time mode.

findings.title: A provisioned Phase 7 image can enable relay before Phase 8 qualification
findings.summary: Phase 4 restores broker relay fallback; Phase 7 permits provisioned hardware readiness; Phase 8 only says default enablement happens afterward. No enforced qualification latch keeps production signing/routing disabled between implementation and physical approval.

evidence.label: Unsafe intermediate state
evidence.explanation: A production-shaped Phase 7 image can have healthy hardware before Phase 8 evidence passes.

evidence.label: Required revision
evidence.explanation: Add independent qualification state. Phase 7 forces remote signing and broker fallback unavailable even with healthy hardware. Phase 8 produces an independently signed product/board/firmware/AP-image/profile tuple; only a later explicit release-manifest change enables it, with protected rollback prevention. Test provisioned-but-unqualified denial.

optionalProperties.release_gate: Provider readiness never implies qualification readiness.

findings.title: Pinned embedded-tls cannot transmit the certificate chain the plan requires
findings.summary: Phase 3 freezes a bounded DER chain, but embedded-tls 0.19 returns one client Certificate and adds one list entry. Phase 4 patches only fallible signing. A leaf-plus-intermediate managed-CA chain cannot execute without another dependency change or an explicit direct-root decision.

evidence.label: Pinned API evidence
evidence.explanation: Reviewed embedded-tls 0.19 defines client_cert() -> Option<Certificate<...>> and calls certificate.add(...) once.

evidence.label: Required revision
evidence.explanation: Add a preflight and pinned API/patch for an ordered bounded certificate list plus fallible signing. Test leaf-only, intermediates, order, missing/duplicate/oversized/truncated chains against the relay. If direct-root issuance is intended, make it an explicit reviewed CA-profile decision.

optionalProperties.release_gate: The exact managed-CA chain completes TLS 1.3 client auth without omission or relaxed validation.

findings.title: The production cryptographic contract is incomplete and partly unverifiable
findings.summary: Phase 1 does not freeze raw/DER or low-S details; Phase 7 references an absent frozen high-S rule. Phase 8 measures entropy failure without a nonce/TRNG/DRBG pass/fail contract, while absolute non-exportability claims exceed readback evidence.

evidence.label: Risk
evidence.explanation: Biased or repeated ECDSA nonces can recover the durable key even without an export API.

evidence.label: Required revision
evidence.explanation: Freeze wire/DER boundary, scalar bounds, low-S policy and vectors in Phase 1. Phase 6 selects approved nonce/TRNG/DRBG behavior. Phases 7–8 require refusal on health failure and KAT, repeated-message, reset/reseed and fault cases. Express non-exportability as scoped architectural, vendor, artifact, memory/transport and readback evidence.

optionalProperties.release_gate: No signature is emitted when nonce/entropy health or canonical-output checks fail.

findings.title: The hardware phases are placeholders rather than executable handoff units
findings.summary: Phase 6 mentions refining Phase 7 but does not require saved Phase 7/8 files to be rewritten/revalidated. Phase 7 uses unnamed modules/tools/firmware and combines transport, firmware, provisioning, update, rollback, rotation, revocation, RMA and physical tests in one unestimated phase. Every effort field is unestimated.

evidence.label: Missing gate
evidence.explanation: Phase 6 can finish with an ADR while checked-in Phase 7/8 remain generic, letting implementation invent protocol and evidence details.

evidence.label: Required revision
evidence.explanation: Make Phase 6 completion conditional on rewriting/splitting Phase 7/8 with exact repos, commits, APIs, paths, owners, state machines, irreversible procedures, harnesses, evidence and estimates; independently re-review the saved revision. Estimate/split over-one-day phases and replace vague software inventories with exact paths.

optionalProperties.release_gate: Phase 7 stays blocked until a saved product-specific plan has no unresolved security/file/evidence choice and passes review.
